memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The priest shall then offer the other as a burnt offering in the prescribed way and make atonement for them for the sin they have committed, and they will be forgiven.'" - Lev 5:10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In the prescribed way. Not in whatever way seemed reasonable. Not according to the priest's preference or the worshipper's creativity.

God gave the pattern, and He expected it to be followed.

That can sound restrictive to modern ears. We prize authenticity and personal expression, and we are suspicious of prescribed anything. But consider what the prescription actually protected. It meant no priest could invent extra requirements. It meant no worshipper could be told his offering was insufficient because someone changed the rules. It meant forgiveness was predictable and available.

Prescription was not a burden on the poor Israelite. It was his security.

The same is true of the gospel. There is one prescribed way to God, and Jesus stated it plainly: I am the way and the truth and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me (Jn 14:6). That is not narrowness for its own sake. It is the certainty that lets us stop guessing.

And then, for the fourth time across these two chapters, God's verdict: they will be forgiven.

Do it God's way, and the outcome is not in doubt.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I try to approach God on terms I have devised rather than the ones He has given?
2. Does the certainty of God's prescribed way give me assurance, or do I still feel uncertain?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You did not leave me guessing how to come to You. I come through Christ, the way You have prescribed, and I trust Your word that I am forgiven. Amen.
